sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Bodyweight Hip Thrust is a foundational glute exercise performed with the upper back resting on a bench and the hips driven up to full extension.

It is the unloaded version of the barbell hip thrust, ideal for learning the movement pattern, building a strong mind-muscle connection, and warming up before heavier work.

Despite using only bodyweight, it produces a strong glute contraction and is suitable for all training levels.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Direct activation of the gluteus maximus
- Reinforces hip extension mechanics for heavier lifts
- No equipment beyond a bench is required
- Excellent warm up for barbell hip thrusts
- Builds glute endurance and tension control
- Beginner friendly with a low learning curve
- Can be progressed with tempo, pauses, or single leg variations

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Gluteus Maximus

Secondary: Hamstrings, Core, Erector Spinae, Quadriceps

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Sit on the ground with your back against a bench.
2. Bend your legs and place your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
3. Confirm the bench is stable before beginning.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Place your shoulder blades against the edge of the bench.
2. Your body should form a straight line from your shoulders to your knees when in the top position.
3. Brace your core and tuck the chin slightly.

sections.heading: Lift
sections.content:
1. Brace your core and drive through your heels.
2. Lift your hips towards the ceiling until your hips are fully extended.
3. Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement for maximum engagement.

sections.heading: Lower and Repeat
sections.content:
1. Lower your hips back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
2. Keep tension in your glutes throughout the descent.
3. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Hyper-extending the lower back at the top
- Pushing through the toes instead of the heels
- Letting the knees cave inward
- Failing to fully extend the hips
- Tucking the chin too aggressively or letting the head drop
- Bouncing the hips off the floor
- Holding the breath through the rep

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Stable bench or sturdy elevated surface
- Athletic shoes for foot traction
- Optional: Mat for floor comfort
- Optional: Mirror to monitor form

sections.heading: Bench Adjustments
sections.content:
1. Place the bench against a wall or weight to prevent it from sliding.
2. Confirm the bench height supports the upper back comfortably.
3. Check that the bench is stable before loading any weight.
4. Choose a slightly padded surface for shoulder comfort if needed.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
2. Torso: Shoulder blades on the bench, ribs stacked, core braced.
3. Knees: Bent at roughly 90 degrees in the top position.
4. Hips: Driven up to full extension, glutes squeezed.
5. Head: Neutral, eyes forward.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Barbell Hip Thrust: Heavy loaded version
- Dumbbell Hip Thrust: Loaded with a dumbbell across the hips
- Glute Bridge: Floor-based hip extension
- Single Leg Hip Thrust: Unilateral variation
- Glute Kick Back Machine: Machine-based glute isolation
- Romanian Deadlift: Compound posterior chain lift

sections.heading: Bodyweight Hip Thrust Variations
sections.content:
Standard Bodyweight Hip Thrust: Described here
Single Leg Hip Thrust: One leg lifted for greater unilateral demand
Feet Elevated Hip Thrust: Feet on a step or box for more glute stretch
B Stance Hip Thrust: One foot lightly placed for unilateral bias
Paused Hip Thrust: Pause at the top for greater glute tension
Tempo Hip Thrust: Slow eccentric for hypertrophy

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Lower Back Pain: Avoid over-extending at the top, focus on glute squeeze
Knee Pain: Adjust foot position to reduce knee strain
No Bench: Perform a glute bridge on the floor instead
Shoulder Discomfort: Use a padded bench edge or towel for the upper back
Balance Issues: Keep the feet wider for stability
Beginners: Start with floor glute bridges before progressing to hip thrusts
